description: The image displays two stacked line plots illustrating the behavior of two variables — $ n $ (top plot) and $ \text{Size}_{\text{rem}} $ (bottom plot) — as functions of a parameter $ m $, which ranges from 0 to $ m_0 $ along the horizontal axis. Both plots share the same x-axis, labeled $ m $, with a linear scale and no explicit tick marks or units, though the endpoint is marked as $ m_0 $. The top plot’s y-axis is labeled $ n $, with key reference levels marked: 0, $ w $, $ c - a - s $, and $ c - a $, suggesting thresholds or constants relevant to the model. The line in this plot is a piecewise linear, sawtooth-like function: it rises linearly from 0 to $ c - a $, then drops sharply to $ w $, and repeats this pattern with decreasing amplitude — the peaks descend from $ c - a $ to $ c - a - s $, then to $ c - a - 2s $, and so on, until the final segment ends at a value just above $ w $. The bottom plot’s y-axis is labeled $ \text{Size}_{\text{rem}} $, with reference levels at 0, $ w + a + s $, and $ c $. The line here also follows a sawtooth pattern: it rises linearly from 0 to $ c $, then drops sharply to $ w + a + s $, and repeats with decreasing peak heights — the first peak is at $ c $, the next at $ c - s $, then $ c - 2s $, etc., ending just above $ w + a + s $. Both plots use solid black lines with sharp vertical drops and linear ascents, visually representing a periodic reset or compression mechanism, consistent with the paper’s theme of segment compression in LLMs.
